rules.title: Mandatory disclosures for rental increases over 10%
rules.requirement: A residential landlord seeking to raise a current tenant’s rent by more than 10% year over year at lease renewal must give specified disclosures before implementing the increase. The disclosures must include an itemization of costs, whether a rent algorithm was used, notice of the tenant’s right to take legal action, and Hoboken Division of Housing contact information.
rules.key_value: More than 10% year-over-year renewal increase triggers disclosures

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies when a residential landlord seeks to increase rent by more than 10% upon renewal of a lease with a current tenant year over year.
coverage.summary: Covers residential landlords in Hoboken seeking more than a 10% year-over-year rent increase for a current tenant at lease renewal.

rules.penalty: A landlord who pleads guilty to or is found guilty of failing to provide the required disclosures is subject to a fine not exceeding $1,000 per incident.
rules.interaction: The required disclosure must tell tenants they may take legal action if they believe the proposed increase is unconscionable or otherwise not in accordance with local or state law.
rules.quoted_span: All residential landlords seeking to increase rent by more than 10% upon a renewal of a lease with a current tenant year over year shall be required to make the following disclosures to existing tenants

rules.title: Algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing market prohibited
rules.requirement: Landlords renting residential dwelling units in Hoboken may not use software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels. Nonpublic competitor information includes prices, supply levels, security deposits, ideal occupancy levels, lease termination or renewal dates, or other material terms that are less than 365 days old and not readily available to the public at no cost.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic price fixing using nonpublic competitor information less than 365 days old

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies to landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit used as a primary residence; excludes medical/long-term care and detention facilities.
coverage.summary: Covers landlords renting residential dwelling units in Hoboken, defined as primary residences other than medical/long-term care or detention facilities.

rules.exemptions: Medical/long-term care facilities and detention facilities are excluded from the definition of residential dwelling unit.
rules.penalty: Upon conviction, a violator is subject to one or more penalties: penalties prescribed under N.J.S.A. 40:49-5, a fine not exceeding $2,000, or community service not exceeding 90 days.
rules.interaction: The ordinance states that penalties may include penalties prescribed under N.J.S.A. 40:49-5.
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.
